findings.explanation: The Splunk Universal Forwarder is downloaded from splunk.com, not Splunkbase, and it has no SNMP polling input; splunkbase.splunk.com/app/617 returns 404.
findings.quote: Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll
findings.suggested_fix: Name the actual SNMP collector: Splunk Connect for SNMP or the SNMP Modular Input (Splunkbase 1537), polling PowerNet-MIB airIRRCUnitStatus and airIRRCGroupSetpoints. Drop the Universal Forwarder and the 617 ID.

findings.explanation: PowerNet-MIB reports InRow supply air temperature and setpoints in tenths of a degree (airIRRCUnitStatusSupplyAirTempUS/Metric, airIRRCGroupSetpointsSupplyAirUS/Metric). Unless values are divided by 10, the 3-degree threshold is really 0.3 degrees and alerts constantly. The implementation should say this.
findings.suggested_fix: State that the raw MIB values are tenths of °F (US) or °C (Metric) and must be divided by 10. Pick one unit family for both supply and setpoint, and give the threshold in that unit.

findings.explanation: SC4SNMP writes polling events as sourcetype sc4snmp:event to index netops by default, while the spl expects sourcetype snmp:apc:cooling in index=cooling with a flat unit_name field. Nothing explains the override. The repository guide lists sourcetype snmp:crac for cooling.
findings.quote: Splunk Connect for SNMP (SC4SNMP) or SNMP Modular Input
findings.suggested_fix: Document how sourcetype snmp:apc:cooling, index=cooling and unit_name (for example from airIRRCUnitIdentName) are produced, or align with the guide's sourcetype.

findings.explanation: The spl uses earliest=-4h, and the HEC and vendor-API troubleshooting doesn't apply to SNMP polling of an InRow cooling unit.
findings.quote: Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h ... inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint
findings.suggested_fix: Match the schedule to the 4-hour window and replace the REST troubleshooting with SNMP polling checks (credentials, UDP 161, PowerNet-MIB loading, and verifying that the supply air and setpoint objects return values for the InRow model family in use: RC, RD or RP).

findings.explanation: These are template scenarios that don't describe a real cause of supply-air deviation.
findings.quote: Batch `avg` on `snmp:apc:cooling` — Scheduled automation elevates `supply` without crossing `delta` > 3
findings.suggested_fix: List real causes: setpoint changes not yet reached, units in standby or idle within an N+1 group, start-up after a unit restart, the group setpoint differing from a unit's local setpoint, and mixing tenths with whole-degree values.

findings.explanation: The SPL reads non-existent MIB objects and unscaled values, so it cannot have been validated.
findings.suggested_fix: Set status to draft or unverified until an SME runs it on InRow data.

findings.explanation: InRow RC units report their own return air and rack inlet temperatures (airIRRCUnitStatusReturnAirTempUS, airIRRCUnitStatusRackInletTempUS), which are more relevant than room CRAH sensors.
findings.suggested_fix: Suggest correlating with the unit's own return and rack-inlet temperatures and fan speed (UC-15.4.7).

findings.explanation: A PDU product page is cited for an InRow cooling UC, and the SC4SNMP link is a Splunkbase search although SC4SNMP is not distributed there.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite the PowerNet-MIB airIRRC definitions and the SC4SNMP docs.

findings.explanation: The detection uses polled values, not traps.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: airIRSupplyAirTemperature and airIRSetpointTemperature are not PowerNet-MIB objects. For InRow RC units, use airIRRCUnitStatusSupplyAirTempUS/Metric and airIRRCGroupSetpointsSupplyAirUS/Metric, all in tenths of a degree, so divide by 10 before 'delta>3' (https://oidref.com/1.3.6.1.4.1.318.1.1.13.3.2.2.2, https://oidref.com/1.3.6.1.4.1.318.1.1.13.3.2.1.2). As written, the threshold is effectively 0.3 degrees.

summary: A supply-air versus setpoint deviation check whose SPL reads invented AirIR object names and ignores the MIB's tenths-of-a-degree scaling, so 'delta > 3' would fire at 0.3 degrees. The surrounding text is template residue.
